checks.label: Are the options expensive?
checks.detail: Option market is charging about 14% expected movement. This stock actually moved about 22% a year pace over the last 20 days. Selling premium only makes sense when the price charged is higher than the movement that usually happens.

checks.label: Did the stock just get stretched? (our best-tested pattern)
checks.detail: Our tests liked selling premium right after a stretch, because stretched moves often calm down. The last finished trading day did not show that stretch, so this would not be our tested pattern.

checks.label: Is the trade on the calm side of the trend?
checks.detail: Price now 758.37, 50-day average 765.00. A put-credit trade wants price above that average; a call-credit trade wants it below.

checks.label: Is the worst case small and known?
checks.detail: Worst case on 1 contract is $424 if everything goes wrong. You collect $76 if you close flat. Never sell options without that protective second leg.

checks.label: Is the strike a reasonable distance away?
checks.detail: The sold option's delta is -0.30. Roughly, traders read 0.30 as about a 30% chance of ending in the money. Much closer than that is gambling, not premium collecting.

PUT.verdict: This does not match our tested pattern.
